messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — region=gcp-europe-north1 impact=private-connectivity latency_tail > 2.5s for multiple customers using MPLS/VPN egress. Auto-alerting oncall. thread=1768459200
Mike (oncall): Acked. Paging netops and runtime. Oncall taking lead.
Julie (netops): I'm on it — pulling BGP session state from our vPC peers and customer interconnects. First look: multiple short BGP withdraws seen from peer 35.204.12.0/29 since 1768459080.
Sara (eng-runtime): Seeing elevated token generation latencies for private deployments in europe-north1. Canary traffic shows 2.8–4s p95 token latency. Metrics: request_queue depth up ~30%.
Sean (support): Customer Ops reporting degraded UX for two enterprise customers with private VPC peering. They're seeing dropped responses and reconnect flaps.
Julie (netops): dumping BGP logs now. snippet:
```
BGP: peer 35.204.12.10 NOTIFICATION (code 3, subcode 4) received
BGP: route withdraw 10.10.0.0/16 from peer 35.204.12.10
BGP: session reset (duration 00:02:13)
```
Julie (netops): Looks like intermittent session resets with our carrier / partner on the interconnect fabric. Possibly MPLS jitter upstream.
Mike (oncall): Any immediate mitigation we can do from our side? Can we shift affected customers to a fallback route/region?
Sara (eng-runtime): Yes — we have smart routing fallback to europe-west2 and europe-west4. We can flip routing policy for pinned private deployments to prefer fallback region via config rollouts. This will add a cold-start model pull for some customers but restores latency.
Sean (support): Notifying customers now that we're investigating and may perform failover to alternate region to mitigate. Will share ETA and impact.
Customer Ops: Please include mention that logs/requests will traverse a different region and that data plane remains encrypted; no config changes required on customer side.
Mike (oncall): Julie, can you confirm if there's a broader GCP maintenance or supplier ISP issue reported?
Julie (netops): Checked GCP status — no public maintenance for europe-north1. Reached out to carrier NOC, they reported 'transport jitter' on a set of circuits since ~09:35 UTC and are investigating.
DeployBot: Automated runbook suggested: "failover-private-egress-to-region". Steps: 1) update routing policy 2) scale up europe-west2 pools 3) toggle canary 4) monitor.
Mike (oncall): Sara, can you start the failover runbook? Prioritize customers with SLA and highest error rates.
Sara (eng-runtime): Starting runbook now. Step 1: bump europe-west2 dedicated pool by +30% for private tenants. Command pasted to Job Runner:
```
# scale job
redwoodctl scale-pool --region europe-west2 --pool private-dedicated --delta 30%
```
Sara (eng-runtime): Step 2: modify routing policy for affected customer route prefix lists to prefer europe-west2 with sticky fallback. Applying patch to config store.
Sara (eng-runtime): Pushing policy patch as canary to 10% of affected tenants.
Mike (oncall): Keep canary for 2 minutes and verify tail latency and 5xx rates. If good, roll to 100%.
Julie (netops): Carrier just responded — investigating flaps on PE -> CE paths, may be a misconfiguration after a recent maintenance window. Could be more withdraws for the next ~10–15m.
Sara (eng-runtime): Canary results after 2m: p95 latency dropped from 3.2s to 0.9s for canary tenants, 5xx rate down to baseline. Proceeding to roll to 100% with automated throttling.
Sean (support): Informing Customer A and Customer B about failover. Messaging: "We have initiated an automated regional failover for private traffic; you may see transient reconnects. We're monitoring and will update."
Mike (oncall): Julie — any risk to data plane integrity during reroute (e.g., asymmetric paths, MTU)?
Julie (netops): MTU differences possible but unlikely to break TLS sessions; we'll watch conn resets. Flow logs show some asymmetric routing but no MTU ICMPs yet.
Customer Ops: Customer A confirms partial recovery on their side after 45s; still seeing sporadic reconnects.
Sara (eng-runtime): Roll complete. All affected private prefixes now prefer europe-west2 as primary, europe-north1 as secondary. autoscaler ensured capacity.
Mike (oncall): Monitoring for 15 minutes. If stable, we'll update incident state to mitigated and start RCA.
Julie (netops): Carrier NOC confirms they applied a rollback on their config which reduced flaps; they're still validating.
IncidentBot: Incident status update — mitigated. affected_regions=[gcp-europe-north1], mitigation=regional_failover_to_europe-west2, severity=high->mitigated, incident_id=INC-2026-1768459.
Sean (support): Customer communication updated: "Impact mitigated via failover; service restored with reroute to europe-west2. We're following up with network partner and will schedule a post-incident call."
Mike (oncall): Handoff to oncall-Sara for the follow-up RCA. I'll remain as incident lead for postmortem. Please gather BGP dumps, carrier comms, and timeline.
Julie (netops): Attaching logs and timeline to the incident ticket (link). Key items: BGP withdraw bursts at 09:34–09:42 UTC, carrier rollback at 09:47 UTC, failover initiated 09:49 UTC, roll complete 09:52 UTC.
Sara (eng-runtime): Noted. Will run canary traffic replay against europe-north1 once carrier confirms fix to validate no residual state issues.
Mike (oncall): Thanks team. Next steps: 1) Confirm permanent routing policy for private tenants (avoid single-region pinning without multi-region fallback) 2) RCA with carrier 3) Postmortem and customer timeline.
Customer Ops: Customers acknowledged. One customer requested a follow-up bridge for postmortem — scheduling.
IncidentBot: Recording incident closure pending postmortem.
DeployBot: If you want to revert routing (move back to europe-north1) run `redwoodctl routing promote --region europe-north1 --tenants <ids>` once carrier confirms stability.
Mike (oncall): End of real-time updates. Marking thread for postmortem collection. Will update ticket with owners and ETA for report. :white_check_mark:
